the molecular mechanisms of transporters, and the role that transporters play in human physiology.
the structure and function of membrane transporters, with particular emphasis on the molecular basis of ligand recognition, transport mechanisms, and regulation of activity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
POT proteins are promiscuous peptide transporters with diverse functions.
the POT family has been studied for over 40 years, yet we are only now starting to understand the molecular basis of its diverse functions.
the family members share a common fold, but have adapted their ligand binding site to accommodate a wide range of ligand chemistries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the POT family is a dynamic and adaptable family of transporters that has evolved in a manner that allows them to recognize and transport a diverse range of substrates.
the POT family has a highly conserved mechanism of ligand recognition, and that this is a major factor contributing to the diverse substrate promiscuities observed in the family.
the POT family is an excellent example of how the evolution of transporters is driven by the need for a cell to acquire new nutrients.
